title: Anatomy of a Prompt: Roles, Templates and Instruction Hierarchy
summary: A chat request is rendered into one long token sequence before the model ever sees it. Knowing how roles, templates and the system prompt turn into tokens tells you what a prompt costs, what the model will prioritise and why instructions get dropped.
objectives: Explain how a chat template renders system, user, assistant and tool messages into one token sequence
Compute the token and cost overhead of a system prompt and of a growing multi-turn conversation
Describe the instruction hierarchy and predict what a model should do when instructions conflict
Estimate the probability that a model follows all of k independent instructions, and use it to decide when a prompt has too many rules
Rewrite a vague prompt into a specific one and justify the extra tokens with expected-retry arithmetic
prerequisites: You should know what a token is and how text is split into tokens ([Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization)), and that a model predicts one next token at a time from everything in its context ([Next-token prediction and sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling)). The idea of a context window from [Context windows and the KV cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache) helps.
